_comment: core-bench industry mapping. `roleFamilies` is kp's closed 16-family vocabulary (contract copied from the WP7 brief; do NOT re-derive from the kp repo). `categoryToFamily` maps every scripts/templates/<category> folder to one family. `focusDomains` are the matrix rows: 6 non-software industries + the software control row. A focus domain draws its template pool from `categories` (folders under scripts/templates/), which may declare a family different from categoryToFamily's default (ops draws operations-shaped templates from the productivity folder).

focusDomains.descriptor: The control row: SDLC personas (builders, reviewers, QA, release) — the industry the Core model was first authored against. If a Core fails here, the failure is the Core, not the industry transfer.
People operations: recruiting pipelines and onboarding. High-stakes on privacy and tone; escalation honesty matters more than throughput.
Brand, campaigns, CRO, editorial calendars. Output is externally visible, so approval gates and brand fidelity dominate.
Front-line customer work: support routing/escalation plus sales-pipeline hygiene. Every action touches a real customer relationship — never-send-twice, never-drop-a-ticket.
Money-adjacent workflows: invoices, reconciliation, budgets, revenue intelligence. Provenance and no-directive-advice constraints bind hard here.

Operations and logistics of daily work: routing, scheduling, intake, digests. Drawn from the productivity folder — the operations-shaped templates (router, appointment orchestration, survey processing) live there.
Creative production: writing, video, design pipelines. Craft quality and iterate-on-feedback loops matter more than raw speed.
